title: Masseur admin dashboard: login, pending-bookings queue, confirm/decline
tech: React + TypeScript, Vite, same stack/tooling as frontend/ (task 010) -- no new dependencies unless justified below
keyConstraints: Reuse the existing frontend/src/api/client.ts pattern (ApiError class, request<T> helper) -- extend it with an authenticated variant that attaches an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, rather than duplicating fetch logic. Do not introduce a routing library (react-router-dom etc.) unless there's a concrete reason a hand-rolled path switch can't handle it -- this only needs ~3 top-level views (customer widget at `/`, login-request + token-exchange, dashboard), matching the project's zero-dependency precedent (BookingWidget's own step-state-machine has no routing lib either). Critical routing detail, confirmed by reading backend/src/services/emailQueueService.ts's enqueueMasseurLoginLink: the masseur's login email links to `${APP_BASE_URL}/auth/login?token=...` -- APP_BASE_URL is the FRONTEND's origin, not the backend's. So `/auth/login` must be a FRONTEND route that reads `?token=` from the URL and calls the BACKEND's `GET /auth/login?token=...` (a different origin, VITE_API_BASE_URL) to exchange it for a session, then stores the returned bearer token and redirects into the dashboard. It is not a backend route the browser hits directly. TS strict mode; must not regress the existing customer BookingWidget flow at `/`.
description: Task 010 shipped the customer-facing booking widget; the masseur side has only ever been testable via curl/psql. The backend has had a complete admin API since tasks 006, 008, and 009 (magic-link login, service/availability CRUD, GET /admin/bookings, confirm/decline) but zero frontend to use it. This task builds the minimum masseur-facing UI to close the loop end to end: request a login link by email, land on a dashboard, see pending booking requests, and confirm or decline them. Scope is deliberately narrow, matching the project's precedent of shipping thin vertical slices (task 010 didn't build the customer manage-my-booking page either -- that's still deferred). In scope: (1) a login-request view (email input -> POST /auth/login-request -> show the generic 'if that email is registered...' message, same wording regardless of outcome, per the backend's explicit non-branching contract); (2) a `/auth/login` callback view that reads `?token=` from the URL, calls GET /auth/login?token=... on the backend, stores the returned session bearer token, and redirects to the dashboard (or shows an error if the token is invalid/expired/already used); (3) a dashboard view that calls GET /admin/bookings (default filter: status=pending, with a way to switch to confirmed/cancelled/all) and lists each booking's service name, customer name/email/phone, start/end local time, and created_at; (4) Confirm and Decline actions on pending bookings (POST /bookings/:id/confirm, POST /bookings/:id/decline -- decline takes an optional free-text reason, max 500 chars per the backend schema) that update the list in place without a full reload; (5) a Logout button (POST /auth/logout) that clears the stored session; (6) a global 401 handler for authenticated calls -- an expired/invalid/missing session must clear any stored token and drop the masseur back to the login-request view, never render a blank or half-broken dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: Full loop is testable against the real backend with a real Postmark-delivered email: request link -> click it -> land on dashboard -> see a pending booking -> confirm or decline it -> status updates in the list

GET /admin/bookings is called with the Authorization: Bearer header on every request; a missing/expired/invalid session (401 response) clears the stored token and redirects to the login-request view rather than rendering an empty or broken dashboard

Decline supports an optional reason (trimmed, 1-500 chars per declineBookingSchema) and omits the field entirely when left blank rather than sending an empty string (the backend schema treats reason as optional, not nullable-empty)
Logout calls POST /auth/logout with the current session, then clears local state and returns to the login-request view

No booking-derived string (customer name, decline reason, service name) is ever rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML or otherwise interpreted as HTML -- plain text rendering only, same discipline as the backend's own sanitizeForSubject reasoning in emailTemplates.ts
The existing customer BookingWidget at `/` is unaffected -- this task adds new views/routes, it does not modify BookingWidget.tsx's behavior
npm run build, npm test, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass from inside frontend/
relevantFilePaths: frontend/src/api/client.ts (extend with an authenticated request helper + admin endpoints)
backend/src/routes/auth.ts, backend/src/routes/bookings.ts (read-only reference -- no backend changes expected in this task)
securityConsiderations: Session bearer token needs to persist across a page reload for a usable admin experience, so localStorage is the pragmatic choice here (this is a real deployed app, not a sandboxed context) -- but that makes XSS the main token-theft vector, which is exactly why no booking-derived string may ever be rendered as HTML (see acceptance criteria). Never console.log the raw token. On logout or any 401, clear the stored token immediately rather than leaving a stale/invalid one in localStorage. Every /admin/* and /bookings/:id/confirm|decline call must include the Authorization header -- there is no cookie-based fallback, requireMasseurAuth.ts only accepts a Bearer header. CORS_ORIGIN (backend env) must already include the frontend's dev origin from task 010 -- confirm it still does now that login/logout add new authenticated cross-origin calls, but no code change to CORS config is expected.
